name: checksum-real-world-testing
details: Comprehensive real-world testing of checksum-based concurrency detection using two separate MCP instances (test-memory-A and test-memory-B) that share the same memory root directory. Tests will validate all scenarios described in CHECKSUM-CONCURRENCY-DESIGN.md.

tasks.name: Sequential Modification Detection
tasks.details:
Test the main benefit: detecting modifications that occur BETWEEN separate operations (not during lock wait)

Scenarios:
1. A reads file → B modifies → A writes (based on stale data) → Error expected
2. A views full file → B str_replace → A str_replace (expecting old text) → Error with current content shown
3. A views with range (not cached) → B modifies → A writes → Should NOT error (partial read not cached)

tasks.name: Successful Operations
tasks.details:
Verify operations succeed when content matches expectations

Scenarios:
1. A reads file → A immediately modifies → Success (checksum matches cache)
2. A reads file → B does nothing → A modifies → Success
3. A creates file → A modifies immediately → Success (checksum cached on create)
4. Fresh operation with no cache → Success (no cached checksum to compare)

tasks.name: Error Message Quality
tasks.details:
Verify error messages show current file contents when concurrent modification detected

Validate:
1. Error message includes 'File has been modified by another process'
2. Current content is shown (truncated if >5000 chars)
3. Truncation indicator present for large files
4. Error message is actionable (tells user to re-read and retry)

tasks.name: File Deletion Scenarios
tasks.details:
Test cache behavior when files are deleted

Scenarios:
1. A reads file → B deletes file → A writes → Appropriate error (ENOENT, not checksum error)
2. A reads file → A deletes file → Cache cleared
3. A deletes file → B tries to access → File not found

tasks.name: Rename Operations
tasks.details:
Test cache invalidation on rename

Scenarios:
1. A reads /memories/old.txt → B renames to /memories/new.txt → A writes to old path → File not found
2. A reads /memories/old.txt → A renames to /memories/new.txt → Cache cleared for old path
3. A renames file → B reads new path → No cache (fresh read)

tasks.name: Multiple File Operations
tasks.details:
Test checksum caching across multiple files

Scenarios:
1. A reads file1 and file2 → B modifies file1 → A writes to file1 (error) and file2 (success)
2. Cache isolation: Operations on different files don't interfere
3. Cache per-path: Same filename in different directories treated separately

tasks.name: Large File Handling
tasks.details:
Test content preview truncation for large files

Scenarios:
1. Create file >5000 chars → B modifies → A writes → Error message truncates content with indicator
2. Verify hash computation time acceptable for typical files (<50KB)
3. Edge case: Very large file (1MB+) - still works, just slower

tasks.name: Directory Operations
tasks.details:
Verify directories are NOT checksummed

Scenarios:
1. A views directory → No cache created
2. B adds file to directory → A views directory again → Success (directories not cached)
3. Operations on files within directories work normally

tasks.name: Edge Cases
tasks.details:
Test boundary conditions and unusual scenarios

Scenarios:
1. Empty file handling (checksum of empty string)
2. File with only whitespace/newlines
3. Unicode content (ensure UTF-8 encoding consistent)
4. Rapid sequential operations (A reads, A writes, A writes again)
5. Same content, different operations (str_replace vs insert vs create)
